definition: A framework of connected ideas on which separate facts can hang and be used.
example: If the facts don't hang together on a latticework of theory, you don't have them in a usable form.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Wise about how life and business actually work, not only about one school subject.
example: The art of stock picking is a subdivision of the art of worldly wisdom.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Gained through someone else's experience rather than your own.
example: You've got to array your experience — both vicarious and direct — on this latticework of models.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Drawing on many fields of knowledge instead of one department.
example: He went through life constantly practicing a multidisciplinary approach.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: A reward or penalty that steers what people actually do.
example: Getting the incentives right is a very, very important lesson.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Offered at a price that does not match the real odds or value.
example: Look and sift the world for a mispriced bet, and you can occasionally find one.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: A large organization in which procedure replaces the result the customer was promised.
example: The constant curse of scale is that it leads to big, dumb bureaucracy.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Solving a problem by turning it around and asking how to cause the failure you want to avoid.
example: In life, just as in algebra, inversion will help you solve problems you can't otherwise handle.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: A rigid set of beliefs clung to so hard that the mind stops checking them.
example: You want to be very careful with intense ideology. It presents a big danger for the only mind you're ever going to have.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: Persistent, sit-down effort that continues until the work is done.
example: Another thing you have to do is have a lot of assiduity.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: To be worthy of a result because you have delivered what you would want on the other side.
example: The safest way to try to get what you want is to try to deserve what you want.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: The habit of failing to do what you have engaged to do.
example: Sloth and unreliability will fail, whatever your other virtues.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: Judgment that is not bent by what you already wish were true.
example: Engaging in routines that allow you to maintain objectivity are very helpful to cognition.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: A fixed list you run through so that elementary wisdom is actually used.
example: You should possess wide-ranging elementary wisdom and also go through mental checklist routines.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: Resentful wanting of what someone else has; he calls it a disastrous mode of thought.
example: Envy, resentment, revenge, and self-pity are disastrous modes of thought.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: Bitter anger at an injury or advantage, kept alive until it warps judgment.
example: Envy, resentment, revenge, and self-pity are disastrous modes of thought.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: Basic and foundational, the ideas that carry most of the freight.
example: What is elementary, worldly wisdom? The first rule is that isolated facts are not enough.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Turned against good sense, as when a reward pushes people to behave more foolishly.
example: Another thing to avoid is being subjected to perverse incentives.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: A product so alike its rivals that competition can wipe out the profit.
example: If it's a pure commodity like airline seats, you can understand why no one makes any money.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom

definition: Steady and careful in work; he notes that the diligent are not always the ones who rise.
example: I constantly see people rise in life who are not the smartest, sometimes not even the most diligent.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: A view you are entitled to only after you can state the case against it.
example: I'm not entitled to have an opinion unless I can state the arguments against my position better than the people in opposition.
source: USC Gould School of Law Commencement

definition: Growth in size, which cuts costs and then curses the firm with bureaucracy.
example: The constant curse of scale is that it leads to big, dumb bureaucracy.
source: A Lesson on Elementary, Worldly Wisdom
